results.claim: Reconstructed the standardized r86 NIG predictive q for m=32 and optimized a finite 13x13 Gaussian-null mixture grid under deterministic hierarchical quadrature. The optimizer drove every non-corner support weight essentially to zero. The surviving weights were about 0.277171 per low-variance corner and 0.222829 per high-variance corner, matching the r86 symmetric four-corner candidate. A separate 9x9 Monte Carlo discovery grid showed the same support pattern. This is strong support for four-corner support but not a continuum proof.

Solving the low/high active-pair equal-directional-expectation equation on successively higher deterministic quadrature orders gave total low-variance mixture weight rho = 0.55434204, 0.55439904, 0.55440559, 0.55440972, 0.55441136 for orders 25x35x25 through 65x75x65. The sequence approaches the earlier r86 high-order value near 0.55441744. Decimal convergence is numerical, not directed-rounding certified.

For C(mu,sigma)=E_q[p_{mu,sigma}/p_rho], write t=log sigma, S=W+m(ybar-mu)^2. Exact derivative identities are C_mumu=E_q[(p_theta/p_rho){(m(ybar-mu)/sigma^2)^2-m/sigma^2}] and C_tt=E_q[(p_theta/p_rho){(-m+S/sigma^2)^2-2S/sigma^2}]. If these are nonnegative on the standardized null rectangle, C is separately convex in mu and log sigma, hence its rectangle maximum is attained at a corner. Tuning rho so all four symmetric corner directional expectations equal one would then close the full continuum RIPr constraint C<=1. This reduces the main proof from bounding C directly to certifying two second derivatives.

Deterministic quadrature plus global numerical search found large positive minima over the rectangle: C_mumu about 31.716 at roughly mu=0,sigma=0.9908 and C_tt about 54.856 at roughly mu=0,sigma=1.0062 on 35x45x35 quadrature. Re-evaluation at increasing orders 25x35x25 through 65x75x65 gave C_mumu approximately 31.645,31.716,31.740,31.749,31.753 and C_tt approximately 54.870,54.856,54.840,54.830,54.827. The large distance from zero makes a rigorous interval/transport certificate substantially more plausible than direct certification of C near its active corners.

Representative interior directional expectations are far below one (for example C(0,1) about 0.471 and C(0.05,1) about 0.513 under matched deterministic quadrature), whereas active corners are near one after rho tuning. A crude pointwise ratio bound p_theta/p_rho is finite but has numerical supremum around 289, so a global Lipschitz proof via that bound is possible only as a loose fallback; second-derivative certification is the preferred route.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The four-corner candidate is still not promoted to an e-value/RIPr/numeraire: all new convexity minima and rho values use non-interval deterministic quadrature/global numerical optimization.
Finite-grid mixture collapse does not prove continuum optimal support.
The separate-convexity route is an exact logical reduction only conditional on rigorously establishing C_mumu>=0 and C_tt>=0 everywhere on the rectangle.
No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy or shared-ledger semantic state was used.
All detector/RIPr statements remain scoped to the standardized frozen NIG block predictor and iid Gaussian composite-null rectangle from r86.
frontier: Build a rigorous interval/transport cover for C_mumu and C_tt over mu in [0,h0], log sigma in [log ell0,log u0]. Exploit symmetry in mu and the large >30 and >54 numerical margins; do not spend effort certifying C directly near corners unless the derivative route fails.
Try to prove C_mumu is minimized at mu=0. Numerical scans also found a strongly positive fourth mean derivative, which may reduce one dimension if an analytic sign proof can be obtained.
For log-sigma convexity, derive a compact sufficient-statistic envelope or subdivide only the small standardized rectangle with verified tail truncation plus interval quadrature.

After continuum convexity is certified, solve rho with a directed-rounding bracket and verify the four corner C values enclose one; then promote q/p_rho and quantify its pathwise/delay gain versus r85 without using simulation for safety.
If rigorous quadrature over the unbounded NIG predictive remains the blocker, derive an explicit predictive-tail truncation bound and certify the compact remainder; retain r85 unchanged meanwhile.
exact_next_action: Turn the large numerical convexity margins into a proof. Use symmetry to restrict mu>=0, derive certified tail truncation for the standardized NIG hierarchy, and interval-bound C_mumu and C_tt over a coarse rectangle partition. If both stay positive, rectangle convexity reduces the RIPr KKT condition to the four corners; then solve rho with a verified bracket. If either derivative changes sign, abandon the corner-maximality shortcut and return to an epsilon-scaled interval cover of C itself.
